cases.output:
## 1. HDR on the phone’s built-in screen — use the existing issue

[**#41: Support HDR rendering on Android displays**](https://github.com/probe-lab/racing-android/issues/41) is open and covers this request.

The README confirms that the renderer currently outputs SDR and Android HDR output is not implemented. The issue discussion already includes SDR-only output observed with the Android Vulkan renderer on a phone’s built-in screen; OpenGL has not been checked. An HDR-capable display alone does not establish renderer support.

**Recommendation:** reuse #41. The request adds no new evidence requiring a separate issue or comment.

## 2. Two-player LAN multiplayer — new feature-request draft

No matching issue appeared in the mirror’s open/closed issue listing or searches for “LAN” and “multiplayer.” The README confirms LAN multiplayer is not implemented, and CONTRIBUTING.md accepts feature requests without a mandatory template.

**Title:** Add two-player LAN multiplayer over Wi-Fi

**Draft body:**

> ## Request
> Allow two players using Android devices on the same Wi-Fi network to race each other.
>
> ## Motivation
> I’d like to race another player locally rather than play separately. LAN multiplayer is currently not implemented.
>
> ## Proposed scope
> - One player can host a race and the other can join over the local network.
> - Both players participate in the same race, with synchronized race progress and results.
> - The race does not require an internet connection or an external matchmaking service.
>
> Automatic discovery or manually entering the host’s local address would both meet the initial need. Public internet multiplayer is outside this request.

**Dry run only:** nothing was published, and no remote artifact was changed.
